The **BenchWeave plugin developer SDK** is the offline toolkit to develop BenchWeave OTDP device plugins. Use it to generate a plugin project. Use it to implement and test the plugin against SDK-supplied interfaces and scripted mocks. Use it to validate descriptor and presentation contracts offline. Use it to prepare a reviewed release. You do not import gateway internals in any of these steps.

The SDK is a separate wheel from the BenchWeave gateway. PyPI publishes it as `benchweave-sdk`. The [main BenchWeave repository](https://github.com/madeinoz67/benchweave) mounts it at `packages/sdk` as a git submodule. The SDK has its own CI and release cycle. Python 3.13+, OTDP 0.2.2 and adapter API 1.1 are the baseline. `pyproject.toml` and the changelog give the SDK's own version. This page does not claim a version.

# Installation

Stable releases are on PyPI:

```sh
pip install benchweave-sdk
# or as an isolated CLI tool
uv tool install benchweave-sdk
# or via Homebrew (macOS and Linux)
brew install madeinoz67/tap/benchweave-sdk
```

For the newest unreleased code, install from the default branch:

```sh
pip install git+https://github.com/madeinoz67/benchweave-sdk.git
```

To do development work on the SDK itself, clone the repository. Then run `uv sync --extra test`.

# Quick start

Generate an independent plugin project with one command:

```sh
benchweave-sdk new plugins/acme/model100 --package benchweave_acme_model100
```

The generator creates a standalone project. The project has a source package, an explicitly synthetic protocol, generated mock and conformance tests, and an `AI-GUIDE.md`. The `AI-GUIDE.md` describes the design, build, test, review and release workflow. The path from there has five steps: install, generate, replace the synthetic protocol with verified device behaviour, run the checks, then prepare and approve a release. The [plugin developer guide](user-guide/plugin-sdk.qmd) walks through each step. The [Get started](user-guide/getting-started.qmd) page walks the full sequence with the exact commands and the expected output.
